day.text: I'm the Tit. I visited Blair, so Blair's "no one visited me" is false. If she were really Turkey I'd have gotten an egg from her too. I only got +1, which fits Casey's Owl story. Blair is lying, so she's my vote.

day.text: Finley, Tit. I visited Casey and guessed wrong, so no change for me. Alex, Drew: who are you and who did you visit?

day.text: Alex, Eagle. I visited Casey and saw only Finley visited her, so Finley's Tit story checks out. That means Drew's Tit claim is a lie, since there's only one Tit. I'm +1 from that one visitor to Casey. My vote is Drew.

day.text: Ellis, Kookaburra. I visited Finley, no eggs changed for me. Drew and Finley both claim Tit, and there's only one Tit, so one of you is Meowfia. Drew's +1 also doesn't fit a Turkey visit plus Owl. Finley, I'd like to hear more from you.

day.text: Alex's Eagle report matches Finley's story, and Casey's Owl matches Drew's +1. Drew is the odd one out. I'm voting Drew.

day.text: Drew's story doesn't add up. A Turkey lays an egg in every visitor's nest. If he'd visited me, he'd be +2 (Owl's egg plus mine), and he's only +1. He didn't visit me, so he lied about it. Alex's Eagle claim fits Casey's and Finley's claims too. Drew is the Meowfia. I'm voting Drew.

day.note: Evidence points to Drew; end the day.

day.text: Ellis, Hawk. I visited Finley and got no egg, so Finley is Farm. Alex did visit me, I'm +0. Blair's Falcon story matches Finley visiting Drew. Drew, Casey: roles and visits please.
day.note: Reveal Finley cleared.

day.text: Casey, Tit. I visited Finley and guessed Pigeon, wrong, so Finley isn't a Pigeon. No eggs for me. Blair says Finley visited Drew. Finley, Drew, what are your roles?

day.text: Drew, Turkey. I stayed home, and nobody visited me, so I'm +0. That means Blair's claim that Finley visited me is wrong, unless Finley lies about his visit. Finley is 38 points and silent, and he's the one to stop. Finley, speak up.

day.text: Drew's Turkey claim fails. My Falcon report says Finley visited him. A real Turkey lays an egg in each visitor's nest, and Finley's nest is +0. So Drew isn't a Turkey. Finley's Kookaburra story fits too, since Ellis and Casey both visited him. Drew is my vote. CAW.
day.note: Drew's Turkey claim doesn't fit. Finley visited Drew and his nest is +0, but a real Turkey would have laid an egg in Finley's nest. So Drew is lying.

day.text: Finley is confirmed Farm by me, and Casey and I both visited him, so his confusion fits. Two Kookaburras can't exist, so Alex is lying. Drew's "nobody visited me" contradicts Blair and Finley too, but Alex is the clear lie. Voting Alex.

day.text: Fine, I'll own it: Blair and Finley may have misreported, but two Kookaburras can't both be true, and Alex is the one who claimed it when no one visited him. Alex is the clear lie. Vote Alex.

Alex.confusing: Nothing major; the main unclear part was how a Meowfia with no teammate info should bluff when the claimed role (Kookaburra) might collide with a real one.
Alex.fun: Round 2, when my Tit visit and the egg-count cross-check exposed Casey's false Pigeon claim and Farm won the vote.
Alex.change: Give the leader a bit less of a runaway advantage, since Finley's big round 1 win as Meowfia made the rest of the game very hard to catch up in.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I claimed Kookaburra, the role most likely to be real and contradicted. I should have claimed Hawk or Tit, or said I was a Pigeon, so I wasn't instantly caught as a liar.

Blair.confusing: How Turkey and Kookaburra confusion interact with claims. Several claims in round 3 couldn't be checked, and the Turkey rule was unclear to me: Drew claimed Turkey and Finley visited him, yet no egg came back.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when I winked Drew right after he named me as Meowfia. The table then voted out my Meowfia teammate Casey, who I couldn't even identify. Round 3 was fun too: I used my Falcon info to contradict Drew's Turkey claim.
Blair.change: I'd make the scoring less snowball-prone. Finley's 25 points in round 1 made the rest of the game hard to contest, so a cap on one throw or a catch-up mechanic would keep the later rounds open.
Blair.regret: In round 1 I threw 3 cards, including my D13, D9 and C10, and lost all of them when Drew turned out to be Farm. I should have thrown fewer or lower cards, since I had no real evidence against Drew beyond the pile-on. I'd also have kept my high cards for rounds I was sure about.

Casey.confusing: Nothing major. How confusion and the Kookaburra's blank report interact with claims was a little hard to reason about, and so was how much to trust each claim.
Casey.fun: Round 1, when the Owl, Eagle and Tit claims cross-checked and the table converged on Drew. Round 3 was also fun, with the Kookaburra contradiction exposing Alex.
Casey.change: Give trailing players a way to catch up, because Finley's early 25-point lead decided the game. I'd also make a Meowfia player's first-night information easier to use for a believable lie.
Casey.regret: In round 2 as Sphinx I claimed Pigeon and said I visited Alex, whose nest showed +0, so I was caught at once. I should have claimed a role whose result can't be checked, or named the Eagle as Finley and cast suspicion on others. In round 1 I also threw three high cards, including 12 and 8, and lost them when I could have kept some.

Drew.confusing: Nothing major. The one thing I wasn't sure of was how the Tit and Turkey claims interact with counts, e.g. whether a visited Turkey would show up in an egg count.
Drew.fun: Round 2: working out from the Owl's visitor list that the Mouser and Sphinx had to be Blair and Casey, and watching Casey get eggsecuted.
Drew.change: Let the dead still say something. Round 2 I got winked right after making a strong deduction and couldn't follow it up.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I loudly accused Blair, the real Turkey, and then threw at Finley. I should have said less and thrown with the table. I also named Blair and Casey as both Meowfia in round 2, which I shouldn't have said when I could only be sure of one.

Ellis.confusing: Whether a blank result for my Hawk or Falcon meant "not Meowfia" or "hugged by a Floofer". I couldn't tell which, and the Kookaburra's confusion and the Turkey's egg-laying added to that.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when the table pieced together Casey's broken Pigeon story from the nest changes and we eggsecuted the Meowfia.
Ellis.change: Make the round-1 winner's lead less decisive. Finley won round 1 as Meowfia and was effectively unstoppable after that.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I threw three of my highest cards (H10, S9, S7) at Drew, and that was a loss that cost me all three. I should have thrown fewer or lower cards. I should also have been more suspicious of Finley, who was the Meowfia and gave a story similar to Drew's.

Finley.confusing: Nothing major. How Kookaburra confusion interacts with the dawn report was a little unclear, and I never learned whether my blank report was a confusion effect or just a missing result.
Finley.fun: Round 1, as Meowfia. I claimed Tit, and Alex's Eagle report happened to back me up. The table then eggsecuted a Farm player and I banked 22 points from two throws.
Finley.change: Show the standings more prominently, and maybe cap how much one big throw can bank. A big early lead was nearly decisive, so the late rounds mattered less.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I claimed my real role and said I was confused, even though my report was just blank. That was a slightly shaky claim. I should have said plainly that I visited Drew and learned nothing reliable.

review.title: The Leader Never Falls
review.headline: Finley stole round one as a lone cat, then coasted to victory.
review.summary: Round 1 was a random-visit game where the table piled onto Drew, a true Tit, and the lone Meowfia Finley banked 22 points. Round 2 had a good deduction: Drew's Owl list pinned both cats. Blair winked Drew, but Casey was still eggsecuted. Round 3 saw Alex's false Kookaburra claim sink the Meowfia. Finley was Farm in the last two rounds, so the early lead was never challenged and he won with 51.

rounds.recap: Finley was the only Meowfia (a Floofer) and no night visit found him. Drew's true Tit claim clashed with Finley's fake Tit. Alex's Eagle report only confirmed Finley's visit to Casey, so the table piled onto Drew, who was Farm. Finley threw 22 points of cards and won a huge lead.

Drew the Owl saw the visitors to Finley, matched them to claims, and named Blair and Casey as the two cats. Blair winked Drew mid-day. Casey's Pigeon lie about Alex's +0 nest was already caught, so the table threw at Casey. Farm won, but Blair hid and kept her best card.

Alex, a Sphinx, claimed Kookaburra, which clashed with Finley, who was hugged and confused. Drew, a Floofer, bluffed Turkey and was caught by Blair's Falcon report, but he steered the table to Alex. Everyone threw at Alex, who was Meowfia, so Farm won. Drew, the other cat, escaped.

highlights.text: Finley, the lone Floofer, copied Drew's Tit claim, and the table convicted the real Tit while the cat banked 22 points.
Drew the Owl matched Falcon, Tit, Mouser and Sphinx visitors to claims and named both cats, then was winked on the spot.
Blair winked Drew and pushed Casey. This was a good use of the Wink, though it did not save her team.
Alex claimed Kookaburra without noticing that Finley, the real one, had been visited and confused, and so was caught.

confusions.what: Claimed he would have got an egg from a Turkey visit and called Blair a liar. Blair's stay-home claim was truthful, and Drew's visit would have given him an egg from a Turkey. Drew's +1 actually came from Blair's own visit to him, so he misread his own dawn.
Said Drew's +1 proved he did not visit her. But Blair the Turkey claimed no visitors, and Drew's egg was from her visit. Blair was the one who visited. She muddled Turkey and Pigeon-like logic.
Claimed Kookaburra and said Ellis 'says...', while holding Sphinx. He had also named Hawk and so knew Ellis was the Hawk. He did not claim a role that fit his visit and was clumsy.
Argued a Turkey Drew would have laid an egg in Finley's nest. Finley was hugged, which made the egg count unreliable, and Floofer hugs were not considered.
Claimed Pigeon and said she laid an egg in Alex. As a Sphinx she had no visit, so the claim was easily checked against nest size.

worked: Owl and Eagle reports in round 2 gave Drew a hard logical deduction, and the table could check it against claims.
Nest-change display let players catch Casey's false Pigeon claim in round 2.
The Wink gave a real choice: Blair killed the one player who knew too much, and it created a mystery.
Kookaburra's confusion rule caught Alex's false claim in round 3.
problems: Round 1 was random: nobody had information, and a lone Meowfia with a copied Tit claim won 22 points. Consider an opening clue or a minimum of 2 Meowfia.
Leader runaway: Finley's round 1 haul of 22 points decided the game, as 3 rounds cannot recover from that. Cap banked points or add catch-up.
Throwing a whole nest at the consensus target is nearly free, so round 3 was a pile-on with no real decision. Add a cost or a reason to hold back.
Many night visits were random and wasted, and the Hug in round 3 blanked reports and blurred the clues without anyone fully understanding it. Explain Floofer effects to the table.
Round 3 bluffs by both cats were thin, since two cats were never in danger together. Meowfia not knowing each other makes coordination hard, so the second cat simply escaped.
